quizzes.stem: A project holds `.claude/commands/deploy.md`, and a teammate then adds `.claude/skills/deploy/SKILL.md`. What does `/deploy` run?

options.a: The skill, since it takes precedence over the older format
options.b: Both, one after the other, with the command going first
options.c: The command, because it was in the project first of the two
options.d: Neither, because the duplicate name is refused outright

explanation.a: The product merged the two formats and gives the skill precedence over a command file of the same name.
explanation.c: Ruled out because "A skill beats a command file of the same name", and the order of arrival plays no part.
explanation.b: Ruled out because the two formats are "one mechanism with the skill format as the richer one", so one name resolves to one definition.
explanation.d: Ruled out because "Existing command files keep working", and a shared name is settled by precedence and not refused.

quizzes.stem: A skill folder sits under `.claude/skills/` in a nested folder two levels below where the session began. When does it become available?

options.a: Never, since only skills at the repository root are read
options.b: At startup, together with the skills at the repository root
options.c: The first time Claude reads or edits a file in that location
options.d: Only after a restart that begins inside that folder

explanation.c: Skills in a lower folder load when Claude first works with a file there.
explanation.b: Ruled out because a lower skill loads "the first time Claude reads or edits a file in that subdirectory", and not at startup.
explanation.a: Ruled out because project skills are found "from the directory where you start and from every parent up to the repository root", and a lower folder loads on first use.
explanation.d: Ruled out because once loaded, the skills "stay available for the rest of the session", with no restart.

quizzes.stem: A skill's header lists `allowed-tools: Read Grep`, and its author expects editing to be impossible while the skill is active. What actually happens?

options.a: Editing is removed from the available tools until the next message
options.b: Changing files remains allowed under the usual permission settings
options.c: Editing runs without any prompt because the skill vouches for it
options.d: Editing is refused because only the two listed tools are permitted

explanation.b: The field pre-approves and restricts nothing.
explanation.a: Ruled out because removal belongs to the other field, which removes tools "from Claude's available pool while this skill is active".
explanation.d: Ruled out because the field "does not restrict which tools are available: every tool remains callable".
explanation.c: Ruled out because "your permission settings still govern tools that are not listed".

quizzes.stem: A skill's text says only 'Use these naming conventions for new endpoints', and its header sets `context: fork`. What does the isolated helper do?

options.a: It reads the whole conversation and applies the conventions to it
options.b: It runs inside the main conversation as if nothing were forked
options.c: It asks the user which endpoint the conventions concern
options.d: It gets guidelines but no assignment, and returns nothing useful

explanation.d: A forked skill's body is its prompt, and guidelines without a task give the helper nothing to do.
explanation.a: Ruled out because the helper "doesn't see your conversation history".
explanation.c: Ruled out because the helper starts from the skill text alone, which "gives it the skill content as its prompt", so it has no one to ask.
explanation.b: Ruled out because the setting "starts a new subagent of the type named in" the agent field, so it does not stay in the conversation.

quizzes.stem: Scenario S2, code generation with Claude Code. A team uses Claude Code for refactoring and tests. A skill explains how an old billing system works, and Claude should consult it when relevant, while typing its name would do nothing useful. Which header line fits?

explanation.c: It hides the skill from the person and leaves it available to Claude, which suits background knowledge.
explanation.a: Ruled out because it does the opposite, so that only the person starts it and "the full skill loads only when you invoke it".
explanation.b: Ruled out because a pre-approval for git commands says nothing about who may start the skill, since the field "Pre-approves the listed tools for the turn that invokes the skill".
explanation.d: Ruled out because `argument-hint` "only shows the expected shape in autocomplete", and a fork would give a background note no task.

quizzes.stem: Scenario S2, code generation with Claude Code. A team uses Claude Code for refactoring and tests. The team's review skill must be unable to change files for the turn that runs it. Which header line does that?

explanation.b: A bare name in the removal field takes the tool out of the pool while the skill is active.
explanation.a: Ruled out because the pre-approval field "does not restrict which tools are available".
explanation.c: Ruled out because `argument-hint` "only shows the expected shape in autocomplete".
explanation.d: Ruled out because "only a bare name removes a tool", so the scoped entry leaves editing in place.

quizzes.stem: Scenario S2, code generation with Claude Code. A team uses Claude Code for refactoring and tests. A command text reads 'Summarise the commits by $ARGUMENTS since yesterday', and a developer runs `/standup ana`. What does Claude receive?

options.a: The sentence unchanged, with the name in a separate note
options.b: The sentence with a blank where the name belongs
options.c: The sentence with the name filled in and a line `ARGUMENTS: ana` after it
options.d: The sentence with the name filled in and nothing appended

explanation.d: The placeholder received the input, so it is substituted and nothing is added.
explanation.a: Ruled out because the placeholder takes "All arguments, as typed" and is replaced in the text.
explanation.b: Ruled out because a blank arises only for a named placeholder without an argument, since an indexed one "stays in the content unchanged", and here the input is given.
explanation.c: Ruled out because the extra line appears only when "no placeholder receives them", and this one did.
